_note: Checks that Story Stage is never an empty backdrop, and times the model calls a turn costs. It mounts the stage before anything has been typed, so the first capture shows the stage as a participant first meets it: the opening narration is spoken by a voice with no sprite of its own, and until the stage kept a character standing between lines there was nobody there at all. Later captures follow one real turn through, past the point where the idle timer used to clear the stage: the cast once faded out with the dialogue box, and then the box retired on its own, leaving a character standing beside an empty panel as though they had said nothing. Reading the captures: presence-01 should show a character on the backdrop with the welcome in the dialogue box, presence-02..04 the reply being spoken, presence-05 that character still standing with their name and line still in the panel. The box only retires when nobody is on stage. The godot log's [budget] lines give the seconds each director, actor and fix call took, which is where a slow turn is accounted for. Costs one turn's worth of model calls, and needs a configured provider plus the optional Story Stage art pack, so it is run deliberately rather than in a suite.
